The campus café launched two AI-powered
robot baristas this week, aiming to reduce wait
times during peak hours. Each robot can brew
50 drinks per hour and accepts mobile payments
only. The $100,000 investment was funded by a
tech grant. Students can customize drinks via an
app, which even allows them to choose latte art
generated by algorithms.
The robots are stationed in two high-traffic spots: one inside the
main student center and the other in the engineering building’s
atrium. These locations were chosen to serve both social spaces and
academic hubs where coffee demand is highest.
“We’re blending convenience with innovation,” said campus café
manager Jordan Lee.
“It’s about creating a futuristic experience.” “I ordered a cappuccino,
and the foam had a smiley face,” said junior Maya Patel. “It’s weird
but fun.”
On launch day, a small group of students protested the replacement
of student workers with robots.
